287	/// The pause token (road map "creator-jobs" TX3b, spec §11 TX-34): a silence
288	/// of more than 1 s between two shown words of one clip, read from the voice
289	/// cache, and the cut that shortens it to 0.2 s each end. Pure: it reads the
290	/// cut's `Table` and its `Context`, no file and no window.
291	///
292	/// **Detection.** Consecutive shown tokens a and b, both editable, in ONE
293	/// instance (`edges`' rule: candidates keyed by clip id and nest path, the
294	/// first whose segment holds the word's start, else the first — so one
295	/// instance is one clip, one nest path and one media). Their source words
296	/// are the media's first words whose `identityTick` is the tokens' `id.source`
297	/// (TX-17: an on-device word's `source` is its moved start). The window opens
298	/// at a's END, not its start, so one silence makes one pause. In the window,
299	/// the longest run of non-speech voice cells (the earliest of equal runs) is
300	/// the silence, extended back over non-speech cells to no earlier than a's
301	/// start (`quietStart`): a recognised end is not moved (TX-19) and often lies
302	/// past the phrase's sound, so the run starts where the speech ends.
303	/// Projected onto the timeline, it is a pause only when longer than
304	/// `pauseLongerThan` of TIMELINE time.
305	///
306	/// **The cut.** The span less `pauseKept` each end, each bound snapped to its
307	/// nearest frame; when b's start lies inside, the cut starts on the frame
308	/// after it, so no word's start is cut. Dropped when that leaves nothing, when
309	/// another shown word's TX-32 extent meets it, or when an unread clip starts
310	/// inside it: a pause's cut never takes a shown word.
311	extension TranscriptCut {
312	
313	    /// A pause is a silence longer than this, in timeline ticks: 1 s.
314	    static let pauseLongerThan: Ticks = ReelTime.perSecond
315	    /// What a pause's cut keeps of it at each end, in timeline ticks: 0.2 s.
316	    static let pauseKept: Ticks = ReelTime.perSecond / 5
317	
318	    struct Pause: Equatable {
319	        /// The shown token before it; the token after is `after + 1`.
320	        let after: Int
321	        /// The silence, in timeline ticks: the run projected, unsnapped.
322	        let span: Range
323	        /// What deleting it cuts, snapped; `cut.end > cut.start`.
324	        let cut: Range
325	    }
326	
327	    struct PausePlan: Equatable {
328	        let range: Range
329	        let clipsAfter: Int
330	        let clipsPeak: Int
331	        let refusal: Refusal?
332	    }
333	
334	    /// Every pause between the table's shown tokens, in ascending `after`.
335	    static func pauses(_ table: Table, fps: Fps) -> [Pause] {
336	        guard table.shown.count > 1 else { return [] }
337	        let context = table.context
338	        struct Key: Hashable {
339	            let clip: UInt32
340	            let nestPath: [UInt32]
341	        }
342	        var byKey: [Key: [Int]] = [:]
343	        for (index, instance) in context.instances.enumerated() {
344	            byKey[Key(clip: instance.clip.id, nestPath: Array(instance.segment.path.dropLast())), default: []]
345	                .append(index)
346	        }
347	        func instance(of word: TimelineTranscript.Word) -> Int? {
348	            let candidates = byKey[Key(clip: word.clip, nestPath: word.id.nestPath)] ?? []
349	            return candidates.first(where: {
350	                let segment = context.instances[$0].segment
351	                return segment.start <= word.start && word.start < segment.start + segment.duration
352	            }) ?? candidates.first
353	        }
354	        // Each media's first source word at a source tick, made once.
355	        var firstAt: [UInt32: [Ticks: Int]] = [:]
356	        func sourceWord(_ word: TimelineTranscript.Word) -> TimelineTranscript.SourceWord? {
357	            guard let heard = context.media[word.media] else { return nil }
358	            if firstAt[word.media] == nil {
359	                var map: [Ticks: Int] = [:]
360	                for (index, source) in heard.words.enumerated() {
361	                    let tick = source.identityTick  // TX-17
362	                    if map[tick] == nil { map[tick] = index }
363	                }
364	                firstAt[word.media] = map
365	            }
366	            return firstAt[word.media]?[word.id.source].map { heard.words[$0] }
367	        }
368	        var out: [Pause] = []
369	        for after in 0..<(table.shown.count - 1) {
370	            let a = table.word(after)
371	            let b = table.word(after + 1)
372	            guard a.editable, b.editable,
373	                let number = instance(of: a), instance(of: b) == number,
374	                let speech = context.speech[a.media],
375	                let aw = sourceWord(a), let bw = sourceWord(b)
376	            else { continue }
377	            let instance = context.instances[number]
378	            let job = instance.job
379	            let low = max(aw.source, aw.sourceEnd, job.sourceIn)
380	            let high = min(max(bw.source, bw.sourceEnd), job.sourceIn + job.sourceLength)
381	            guard let run = longestQuietRun(speech, from: low, to: high) else { continue }
382	            let quiet = quietStart(speech, runStart: run.start, floor: max(aw.source, job.sourceIn))
383	            let shift = instance.segment.origin.map { $0 - instance.clip.start } ?? 0
384	            let span = Range(
385	                start: MediaTranscript.project(quiet, in: job) + shift,
386	                end: MediaTranscript.project(run.end, in: job) + shift)
387	            guard span.end - span.start > pauseLongerThan else { continue }
388	            var s = max(0, ReelTime.snapToFrame(span.start + pauseKept, fps: fps))
389	            let e = max(0, ReelTime.snapToFrame(span.end - pauseKept, fps: fps))
390	            if s <= b.start, b.start < e {
391	                let past = TimelineTranscript.frameFloor(b.start, fps: fps) + max(1, fps.frameDuration)
392	                s = ReelTime.snapToFrame(past, fps: fps)
393	            }
394	            guard e > s else { continue }
395	            let before = after > 0 && table.reachBefore[after - 1] > s

title: "The in/out range"
description: Mark a span of the timeline with I and O, so Loop, deletes, exports and other commands work on that passage alone.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The in/out range marks one passage of the timeline. Set it when you want to loop a section, cut it out, export it on its own, or point another command at it.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Mark ▸ Set In', 'Mark ▸ Set Out', 'Mark ▸ Clear Range']}
  keys={['I', 'O', '⌥X']}
  where="Shaded across the timeline's ruler and lanes"
  tools="set_range"
/>

## Set In

Move the playhead to where the passage starts and press <kbd>I</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set In**. With no range yet, the out point goes to the end of the timeline, so the range runs from the playhead to the end.

## Set Out

Move the playhead to where the passage ends and press <kbd>O</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set Out**. With no range yet, the in point goes to the start of the timeline.

<kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> are bare keys, so the menu shows no shortcut beside them, and they don't fire while you're typing in a field. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).

## Clear Range

Press <kbd>⌥X</kbd> or choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range**. The item is available only while a range is set.

## What the range is

The range is a span shaded across the ruler and the lanes. It changes nothing by itself. These commands read it:

---
title: "Cut by deleting words"
description: Select words in the Transcript tab and delete them, taking the picture and sound under them out of the timeline and closing the gap.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Editing a spoken video can work like editing text. Select words in the Transcript tab, press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, and the words and everything under them come out of the timeline, with the gap closed.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, read on this Mac or from an AssemblyAI transcript. Cutting them uploads nothing."
/>

## Delete words

<Steps>

1. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>). The Transcript tab opens and its text takes the keyboard.

2. [Select the words](#select-words) you want gone.

3. Look at what's shaded on the timeline. That's exactly what will go. To hear it first, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/), which plays the shaded range.

4. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.

</Steps>

The words and the sound under them come out of every unlocked track and the gap closes, as one undo step named **Delete Words**. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.

<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** all do the same thing here. On the timeline, <kbd>⌫</kbd> [leaves a gap](/editing/delete-clips/). In the transcript it closes the gap, the way deleting text does.

Deleting words one at a time gives the same result as deleting them together, unless a pause of more than a second lies between them. See [where a word cut falls](#where-a-word-cut-falls).

:::caution
These keys cut words only while the transcript text has the keyboard. If the timeline has it, <kbd>⌫</kbd> does what it does there: with no clip selected, it lifts the shaded range and leaves a gap. Click in the text first.
:::

## Select words

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Select one word | Click it. The playhead moves to it too. |
| Select a run of words | Drag across them. The text scrolls as you go, and a drag selects words only, never a pause. |
| Extend the selection | <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a word, or press <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow. Neither moves the playhead. |
| Select every word | Press <kbd>⌘A</kbd>. |
| Clear the selection | Press <kbd>⎋</kbd>. |

[Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/) has every key the text takes.

## The selection becomes the range

Whatever you select becomes the timeline's [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), replacing any range you had, so the timeline shades exactly what will go. With the range set you can [loop](/timeline/loop/) or [export](/export/range/) just those words.

The selection can grow as it does this. It widens to whole words and frame boundaries, and over any word the cut would cut into, so what's highlighted is what the cut takes.

<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range with it. It clears only a range the selection set: if you've changed the range since, with <kbd>I</kbd>, <kbd>O</kbd> or an agent, the transcript leaves it alone.

## Where a word cut falls

A cut runs from where the first word starts to where the next word you keep starts. The pause before the cut stays, and the pause after it goes.

- **A long pause after the words.** The cut goes no more than one second past the end of the last deleted word, and the rest of the pause stays.
- **Frames.** Both ends land on whole frames, and the end never passes the start of a word that stays.
- **The last word on the timeline.** With no word after it, the cut ends where the word ends.
- **A clip not read yet.** The cut stops at the start of a clip whose words haven't been read.

## Where a word starts

This Mac's recogniser puts a word's start early, often well inside the pause before it. So the tab moves each start to where its sound begins:

1. It finds where the voice model, the one [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses, first hears speech after the recogniser's start.
2. It then looks for the first hundredth of a second loud enough to be the word: at least −40 dBFS, and 12 dB above the pause's own background noise. The search starts about 0.1 s before the speech, so a click earlier in the pause isn't taken for the word. If nothing is that loud, the start stays where the voice model heard speech.

A word after a pause therefore starts on its sound, so deleting the word before it neither keeps a slice of the pause nor takes the start of the word you keep.

Both steps are worked out when the project opens a file. Until the voice model has heard a file, the starts are the recogniser's own. The tab moves them as soon as it has, and keeps your selection.

Words from an [AssemblyAI transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/), and where any word ends, are left as transcribed.

## How exact a word cut is

Word edges come from the transcript itself, so in fast speech a cut can take the very end of the word before it, or leave a sliver of the word you deleted. Play the shaded range with [Loop](/timeline/loop/) before you delete, and undo if the cut sounds wrong.

## Overlapping words on other tracks

If a word on another track starts before your selection and runs into it, say two people talking at once, the tab adds that word to the selection first, along with any words between. You see everything the cut takes before you press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.

A word on another track that starts inside your last selected word isn't added. It's the next word you keep, so the cut ends at its start, and the rest of the deleted word after that point can stay in.

Only the words the tab shows are added. With **Words from** set to one track, the cut still goes through the other unlocked tracks, and any words it takes there are ones you can't see.

## Words that can't be cut

Some words are shown faint, because a cut at them would break something. Hold the pointer over one to read why.

| Where the word is | What the tab says |
| --- | --- |
| Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) | "Inside nest *name*: open it (⌘↓) to cut its words." |
| Under a [transition](/editing/transitions/) | "Under a transition: a cut here would leave one clip's tail under its neighbour." |
| On a locked track | "Track *name* is locked: a cut would leave these words in place and move everything after them." |

title: "Cut by deleting words"
description: Select words in the Transcript tab and delete them, taking the picture and sound under them out of the timeline and closing the gap.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Editing a spoken video can work like editing text. Select words in the Transcript tab, press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, and the words and everything under them come out of the timeline, with the gap closed.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, read on this Mac or from an AssemblyAI transcript. Cutting them uploads nothing."
/>

## Delete words

<Steps>

1. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>). The Transcript tab opens and its text takes the keyboard.

2. [Select the words](#select-words) you want gone.

3. Look at what's shaded on the timeline. That's exactly what will go. To hear it first, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/), which plays the shaded range.

4. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.

</Steps>

The words and the sound under them come out of every unlocked track and the gap closes, as one undo step named **Delete Words**. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.

<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** all do the same thing here. On the timeline, <kbd>⌫</kbd> [leaves a gap](/editing/delete-clips/). In the transcript it closes the gap, the way deleting text does.

Deleting words one at a time gives the same result as deleting them together, unless a pause of more than a second lies between them. See [where a word cut falls](#where-a-word-cut-falls).

:::caution
These keys cut words only while the transcript text has the keyboard. If the timeline has it, <kbd>⌫</kbd> does what it does there: with no clip selected, it lifts the shaded range and leaves a gap. Click in the text first.
:::

## Select words

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Select one word | Click it. The playhead moves to it too. |
| Select a run of words | Drag across them. The text scrolls as you go, and a drag selects words only, never a pause. |
| Extend the selection | <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a word, or press <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow. Neither moves the playhead. |
| Select every word | Press <kbd>⌘A</kbd>. |
| Clear the selection | Press <kbd>⎋</kbd>. |

[Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/) has every key the text takes.

## The selection becomes the range

Whatever you select becomes the timeline's [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), replacing any range you had, so the timeline shades exactly what will go. With the range set you can [loop](/timeline/loop/) or [export](/export/range/) just those words.

The selection can grow as it does this. It widens to whole words and frame boundaries, and over any word the cut would cut into, so what's highlighted is what the cut takes.

<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range with it. It clears only a range the selection set: if you've changed the range since, with <kbd>I</kbd>, <kbd>O</kbd> or an agent, the transcript leaves it alone.

## Where a word cut falls

A cut runs from where the first word starts to where the next word you keep starts. The pause before the cut stays, and the pause after it goes.

- **A long pause after the words.** The cut goes no more than one second past the end of the last deleted word, and the rest of the pause stays.
- **Frames.** Both ends land on whole frames, and the end never passes the start of a word that stays.
- **The last word on the timeline.** With no word after it, the cut ends where the word ends.
- **A clip not read yet.** The cut stops at the start of a clip whose words haven't been read.

## Where a word starts

This Mac's recogniser puts a word's start early, often well inside the pause before it. So the tab moves each start to where its sound begins:

1. It finds where the voice model, the one [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses, first hears speech after the recogniser's start.
2. It then looks for the first hundredth of a second loud enough to be the word: at least −40 dBFS, and 12 dB above the pause's own background noise. Word edges come from the transcript itself, so in fast speech a cut can take the very end of the word before it, or leave a sliver of the word you deleted. Play the shaded range with [Loop](/timeline/loop/) before you delete, and undo if the cut sounds wrong.

---
title: "Shorten a pause"
description: Spot long pauses in the Transcript tab and tighten them, keeping 0.2 s at each end and closing the gap on every unlocked track.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Transcript tab marks each long pause in the speech. Click one and delete it to tighten the pause without taking any words, as one undo step.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, and the voice model, which runs on your Mac with no key and no upload."
/>

## Pauses in the transcript

Where the speech stops for more than a second between two words of one clip, the transcript shows the pause's length in grey after the word before it, such as `[2.4 s]`.

The length is what the voice model hears as silence between that word and the next. The model is the one [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses. It runs when the project opens the file, so a file's pauses appear once it has finished. They appear for words from an [AssemblyAI transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) as well as words read on this Mac.

The second is measured on the timeline, so a clip's speed changes what counts. A 0.8 s silence in a clip slowed to half speed plays for 1.6 s, and shows as a pause.

## Select a pause

Click the pause. It's selected on its own, the part that would go becomes the timeline's [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), and the playhead moves to the start of that cut. To hear what would go, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/).

<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range. Dragging, <kbd>⇧</kbd> and <kbd>⌘A</kbd> select words only, so a pause is always selected by clicking it.

## Delete the pause

<Steps>

1. Click the pause.

2. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.

</Steps>

The pause is shortened, keeping 0.2 s at each end, and the gap closes on every unlocked track, as one undo step named **Delete Pause**. A `[2.4 s]` pause loses about 2 s and leaves about 0.4 s. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.

<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** do the same, as long as the transcript text has the keyboard.

The cut lands on whole frames and never takes the start of a word.

The tab won't cut a pause when a locked track has words inside the cut, or when the cut would pass the limit of 4,096 clips. It beeps and shows the same [reason](/captions/delete-words/#when-the-tab-refuses-a-cut) it gives for words, at the foot of the inspector.

## When a pause isn't shown

The tab shows a pause only when it can cut it cleanly. There's no pause marked:

- between two clips, including the two halves of a clip you've split
- when either word next to it is [faint](/captions/delete-words/#words-that-cant-be-cut): inside a nest, under a transition or on a locked track
- when a word on another track falls inside it, because the cut would take that word
- when a clip whose words haven't been read yet starts inside the cut
- when keeping 0.2 s at each end would leave nothing to cut

## With an agent

`get_timeline_transcript` reads the same pauses, each with the range the tab would cut it by, and one `ripple_delete_ranges` call shortens one. An agent can pass several in that call, which makes them one undo step. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)
- [Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/)
- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)

---
title: "Transcript keys"
description: Every key the Transcript tab's text takes, for moving by word or line, selecting, clearing and deleting, and what the rest of the keyboard does there.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

While the transcript text has the keyboard, the arrows move through the words instead of the frames, and the delete keys cut words. Every other key works as it does on the timeline.

<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Transcript" keys="⌃⌘T" where="Inspector ▸ Transcript, with the text active" />

To give the text the keyboard, choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>) or click in the text. Clicking **Transcript** in the inspector's tab strip shows the tab but leaves the keyboard where it was.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Select the previous or next word and move the playhead to it |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Select the nearest word on the line above or below and move the playhead to it |
| <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow | Extend the selection without moving the playhead |
| <kbd>⌘A</kbd> | Select every word |
| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Clear the selected words or pause |
| <kbd>⌫</kbd> <kbd>⌦</kbd> | Delete the selected words and close the gap, or shorten the selected pause |

## Move word by word

<kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> select the previous or next word and move the playhead to it. If the video is playing, it keeps playing from there.

They move from the end of the selection you last moved. With a [pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/) selected, they move from the word before it. With nothing selected, they move from the word under the playhead, and if there isn't one, <kbd>→</kbd> selects the first word and <kbd>←</kbd> the last. At the first and last word they stay put.

## Move line by line

<kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> select the nearest word on the line above or below, as the text is laid out, and move the playhead to it. They skip the timecode lines, and beep at the first and last line.

## Extend the selection

<kbd>⇧</kbd> with any arrow moves one end of the selection and leaves the playhead where it is. The other end stays where you started, so going back the other way shrinks the selection. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click does the same with the mouse.

The tab may [widen the selection](/captions/delete-words/#the-selection-becomes-the-range) further, over any word the cut would cut into.

## Select every word

<kbd>⌘A</kbd> selects every word, and **Edit ▸ Select All** does the same while the text has the keyboard. It selects words only, so a selected pause is dropped.

## Clear the selection

<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selected words or pause, along with the range they set. With nothing selected, the key passes up to the window, where it deselects a selected [action](/motion/actions/).

## Delete

With words selected, <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd> [deletes them and closes the gap](/captions/delete-words/). With a pause selected, either one [shortens it](/captions/shorten-pauses/). <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> does the same.

With nothing selected in the text, these keys do what they do on the timeline, so they act on the [selected clips or the range](/editing/delete-clips/).

## Timeline keys keep working

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play and pause |
| <kbd>J</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> <kbd>L</kbd> | Shuttle back, pause, shuttle forward |
| <kbd>I</kbd> <kbd>O</kbd> | Set the in and out points at the playhead |
| <kbd>M</kbd> | Add a marker |

These are the common ones. Any key this page doesn't list works as it does on the timeline. See [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/).

## Related

- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)
- [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/)
- [Follow along and jump](/captions/follow-the-transcript/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)

---
title: "Cut by deleting words"
description: Select words in the Transcript tab and delete them, taking the picture and sound under them out of the timeline and closing the gap.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Editing a spoken video can work like editing text. Select words in the Transcript tab, press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, and the words and everything under them come out of the timeline, with the gap closed.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, read on this Mac or from an AssemblyAI transcript. Cutting them uploads nothing."
/>

## Delete words

<Steps>

1. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>). The Transcript tab opens and its text takes the keyboard.

2. [Select the words](#select-words) you want gone.

3. Look at what's shaded on the timeline. That's exactly what will go. To hear it first, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/), which plays the shaded range.

4. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.

</Steps>

The words and the sound under them come out of every unlocked track and the gap closes, as one undo step named **Delete Words**. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.

<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** all do the same thing here. On the timeline, <kbd>⌫</kbd> [leaves a gap](/editing/delete-clips/). In the transcript it closes the gap, the way deleting text does.

Deleting words one at a time gives the same result as deleting them together, unless a pause of more than a second lies between them. See [where a word cut falls](#where-a-word-cut-falls).

:::caution
These keys cut words only while the transcript text has the keyboard. If the timeline has it, <kbd>⌫</kbd> does what it does there: with no clip selected, it lifts the shaded range and leaves a gap. Click in the text first.
:::

## Select words

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Select one word | Click it. The playhead moves to it too. |
| Select a run of words | Drag across them. The text scrolls as you go, and a drag selects words only, never a pause. |
| Extend the selection | <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a word, or press <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow. Neither moves the playhead. |
| Select every word | Press <kbd>⌘A</kbd>. |
| Clear the selection | Press <kbd>⎋</kbd>. |

[Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/) has every key the text takes.

## The selection becomes the range

Whatever you select becomes the timeline's [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), replacing any range you had, so the timeline shades exactly what will go. With the range set you can [loop](/timeline/loop/) or [export](/export/range/) just those words.

The selection can grow as it does this. It widens to whole words and frame boundaries, and over any word the cut would cut into, so what's highlighted is what the cut takes.

<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range with it. It clears only a range the selection set: if you've changed the range since, with <kbd>I</kbd>, <kbd>O</kbd> or an agent, the transcript leaves it alone.

## Where a word cut falls

A cut runs from where the first word starts to where the next word you keep starts. The pause before the cut stays, and the pause after it goes.

- **A long pause after the words.** The cut goes no more than one second past the end of the last deleted word, and the rest of the pause stays.
- **Frames.** Both ends land on whole frames, and the end never passes the start of a word that stays.
- **The last word on the timeline.** With no word after it, the cut ends where the word ends.
- **A clip not read yet.** The cut stops at the start of a clip whose words haven't been read.

## Where a word starts

This Mac's recogniser puts a word's start early, often well inside the pause before it. So the tab moves each start to where its sound begins:

1. It finds where the voice model, the one [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses, first hears speech after the recogniser's start.
2. It then looks for the first hundredth of a second loud enough to be the word: at least −40 dBFS, and 12 dB above the pause's own background noise. The search starts about 0.1 s before the speech, so a click earlier in the pause isn't taken for the word. If nothing is that loud, the start stays where the voice model heard speech.

A word after a pause therefore starts on its sound, so deleting the word before it neither keeps a slice of the pause nor takes the start of the word you keep.

Both steps are worked out when the project opens a file. Until the voice model has heard a file, the starts are the recogniser's own. The tab moves them as soon as it has, and keeps your selection.

Words from an [AssemblyAI transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/), and where any word ends, are left as transcribed.

## How exact a word cut is

Word edges come from the transcript itself, so in fast speech a cut can take the very end of the word before it, or leave a sliver of the word you deleted. Play the shaded range with [Loop](/timeline/loop/) before you delete, and undo if the cut sounds wrong.

## Overlapping words on other tracks

If a word on another track starts before your selection and runs into it, say two people talking at once, the tab adds that word to the selection first, along with any words between. You see everything the cut takes before you press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.

A word on another track that starts inside your last selected word isn't added. It's the next word you keep, so the cut ends at its start, and the rest of the deleted word after that point can stay in.

Only the words the tab shows are added. With **Words from** set to one track, the cut still goes through the other unlocked tracks, and any words it takes there are ones you can't see.

## Words that can't be cut

Some words are shown faint, because a cut at them would break something. Hold the pointer over one to read why.

| Where the word is | What the tab says |
| --- | --- |
| Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) | "Inside nest *name*: open it (⌘↓) to cut its words." |
| Under a [transition](/editing/transitions/) | "Under a transition: a cut here would leave one clip's tail under its neighbour." |
| On a locked track | "Track *name* is locked: a cut would leave these words in place and move everything after them." |

A nest or track with no name is given by its number. With a nest open, the tab shows only what's inside it, and those words can be cut.

You can still click a faint word to move the playhead there, but a selection that holds one can't be deleted. A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/) isn't faint: its words can be cut.

## When the tab refuses a cut

In these cases the tab beeps, keeps your selection and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after the word "Refused:". The message stays until the project changes or you click it.

| Why | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| A selected word is [faint](#words-that-cant-be-cut). | That word's own reason. |
| A locked track has words inside the cut, even a track **Words from** is hiding. A locked track never moves, so its words would fall out of step. | "Track Music is locked and has words in this cut: unlock it to cut here." |
| The cut would pass the project's limit of 4,096 clips while it's being made. Every clip the cut crosses is split first, so a project near the limit can pass it for a moment even if the cut ends with fewer. | "This cut would make 4097 clips; a project holds at most 4096. Lock a track that needs no cut, such as a music bed, or cut less." |

Closing the gap can also fail for a reason of its own, such as a linked clip that would have to start before 0. That reason shows in the same place.

## Good to know

- The cut goes through everything on every unlocked track, including music, captions and tracks you've muted or hidden. A locked track with no words in the cut stays whole and doesn't move, which is the way to keep a music bed in one piece.
- Markers don't move, as with every [ripple delete](/editing/delete-clips/).

## With an agent

`get_timeline_transcript` reads the same words, says which can't be cut and why, and gives the range the tab would cut each word by. One `ripple_delete_ranges` call from the first word to the last cuts a run. `get_transcript` reads one clip's words. Neither reading tool uploads anything. If the voice model hasn't heard a file yet, the answer has a note saying its starts are still early, so ask again once it has. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/)
- [Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/)
- [The Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/)
- [Where the transcript's words come from](/captions/transcript-words/)
- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
- [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/)

---
title: "Shorten a pause"
description: Spot long pauses in the Transcript tab and tighten them, keeping 0.2 s at each end and closing the gap on every unlocked track.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Transcript tab marks each long pause in the speech. Click one and delete it to tighten the pause without taking any words, as one undo step.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, and the voice model, which runs on your Mac with no key and no upload."
/>

## Pauses in the transcript

Where the speech stops for more than a second between two words of one clip, the transcript shows the pause's length in grey after the word before it, such as `[2.4 s]`.

The length is what the voice model hears as silence between that word and the next. The model is the one [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses. It runs when the project opens the file, so a file's pauses appear once it has finished. They appear for words from an [AssemblyAI transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) as well as words read on this Mac.

The second is measured on the timeline, so a clip's speed changes what counts. A 0.8 s silence in a clip slowed to half speed plays for 1.6 s, and shows as a pause.

## Select a pause

Click the pause. It's selected on its own, the part that would go becomes the timeline's [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), and the playhead moves to the start of that cut. To hear what would go, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/).

<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range. Dragging, <kbd>⇧</kbd> and <kbd>⌘A</kbd> select words only, so a pause is always selected by clicking it.

## Delete the pause

<Steps>

1. Click the pause.

2. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.

</Steps>

The pause is shortened, keeping 0.2 s at each end, and the gap closes on every unlocked track, as one undo step named **Delete Pause**. A `[2.4 s]` pause loses about 2 s and leaves about 0.4 s. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.

<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** do the same, as long as the transcript text has the keyboard.

The cut lands on whole frames and never takes the start of a word.

The tab won't cut a pause when a locked track has words inside the cut, or when the cut would pass the limit of 4,096 clips. It beeps and shows the same [reason](/captions/delete-words/#when-the-tab-refuses-a-cut) it gives for words, at the foot of the inspector.

## When a pause isn't shown

The tab shows a pause only when it can cut it cleanly. There's no pause marked:

- between two clips, including the two halves of a clip you've split
- when either word next to it is [faint](/captions/delete-words/#words-that-cant-be-cut): inside a nest, under a transition or on a locked track
- when a word on another track falls inside it, because the cut would take that word
- when a clip whose words haven't been read yet starts inside the cut
- when keeping 0.2 s at each end would leave nothing to cut

## With an agent

`get_timeline_transcript` reads the same pauses, each with the range the tab would cut it by, and one `ripple_delete_ranges` call shortens one. An agent can pass several in that call, which makes them one undo step. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)
- [Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/)
- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)

---
title: "Transcript keys"
description: Every key the Transcript tab's text takes, for moving by word or line, selecting, clearing and deleting, and what the rest of the keyboard does there.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

While the transcript text has the keyboard, the arrows move through the words instead of the frames, and the delete keys cut words. Every other key works as it does on the timeline.

<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Transcript" keys="⌃⌘T" where="Inspector ▸ Transcript, with the text active" />

To give the text the keyboard, choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>) or click in the text. Clicking **Transcript** in the inspector's tab strip shows the tab but leaves the keyboard where it was.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Select the previous or next word and move the playhead to it |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Select the nearest word on the line above or below and move the playhead to it |
| <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow | Extend the selection without moving the playhead |
| <kbd>⌘A</kbd> | Select every word |
| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Clear the selected words or pause |
| <kbd>⌫</kbd> <kbd>⌦</kbd> | Delete the selected words and close the gap, or shorten the selected pause |

## Move word by word

<kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> select the previous or next word and move the playhead to it. If the video is playing, it keeps playing from there.

They move from the end of the selection you last moved. With a [pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/) selected, they move from the word before it. With nothing selected, they move from the word under the playhead, and if there isn't one, <kbd>→</kbd> selects the first word and <kbd>←</kbd> the last. At the first and last word they stay put.

## Move line by line

<kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> select the nearest word on the line above or below, as the text is laid out, and move the playhead to it. They skip the timecode lines, and beep at the first and last line.

## Extend the selection

<kbd>⇧</kbd> with any arrow moves one end of the selection and leaves the playhead where it is. The other end stays where you started, so going back the other way shrinks the selection. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click does the same with the mouse.

The tab may [widen the selection](/captions/delete-words/#the-selection-becomes-the-range) further, over any word the cut would cut into.

## Select every word

<kbd>⌘A</kbd> selects every word, and **Edit ▸ Select All** does the same while the text has the keyboard. It selects words only, so a selected pause is dropped.

## Clear the selection

<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selected words or pause, along with the range they set. With nothing selected, the key passes up to the window, where it deselects a selected [action](/motion/actions/).

## Delete

With words selected, <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd> [deletes them and closes the gap](/captions/delete-words/). With a pause selected, either one [shortens it](/captions/shorten-pauses/). <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> does the same.

With nothing selected in the text, these keys do what they do on the timeline, so they act on the [selected clips or the range](/editing/delete-clips/).

## Timeline keys keep working

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play and pause |
| <kbd>J</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> <kbd>L</kbd> | Shuttle back, pause, shuttle forward |
| <kbd>I</kbd> <kbd>O</kbd> | Set the in and out points at the playhead |
| <kbd>M</kbd> | Add a marker |

These are the common ones. Any key this page doesn't list works as it does on the timeline. See [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/).

## Related

- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)
- [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/)
- [Follow along and jump](/captions/follow-the-transcript/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
